findings.title: Legacy key and optional-user checks do not form a safe tenant boundary
findings.detail: verify_api_key accepts any nonempty Bearer token; check_rate_limit returns True. Optional-user helper returns None for missing/invalid credentials; some system result/download/delete handlers only enforce ownership if a user object exists. Upstream default auth disabled. This is reference-code risk, not an active product vulnerability claim.
findings.recommendation: Keep inactive; use first-party API owner/digest/rate-limit/reconciliation boundary as canonical. Do not restore upstream public auth or system admin routes wholesale.

findings.title: Upload metadata is not tenant-scoped and existing filesystem paths are accepted
findings.detail: Upload/list/delete/resolve route layer lacks owner credentials in signatures/metadata; process_file_input accepts arbitrary existing image/mesh path with no approved-root check. Whole-upload write precedes size rejection; base64 path decodes full input without equivalent maximum. Mesh parsing can invoke external-format parsers.
findings.recommendation: Keep operator-only upstream private. Use first-party bounded normalized uploads and owner-specific object records; add format resource/sandbox boundaries before any selective reuse.

findings.title: Checkpoint loading and hidden remote resources need separate qualification
findings.detail: UniRig explicitly uses weights_only=False; other helpers use torch.load without explicit safe loading and no full artifact hash guards. Pipelines can download remote pretrained models/configs (including FLUX.1-Fill-dev and rembg/DINO dependencies); heavyweight GPU/backend libraries are not part of the first-party CPU setup. PartPacker explicitly uses weights_only=True, so not every loader has the same weakness.
findings.recommendation: Use isolated approved model runtimes and immutable independently verified inputs; preserve first-party TripoSR preparation as canonical hardening path.

findings.title: Unsafe deployment and install defaults are reference-only
findings.detail: Auth disabled defaults, wildcard CORS, all-interface API/Redis port publication, broad GPU selection and mutable Git/package/model downloads. Download verify functions inspect size/presence/count rather than independent cryptographic integrity. No paid infrastructure or scripts executed by review.
findings.recommendation: Do not enable legacy launch instructions. Review packages, bindings, authentication and checksums in an isolated candidate before any future use.

findings.title: Password hashes are unsuitable as public identity implementation
findings.detail: One SHA256 pass plus salt and six-character minimum, instead of a reviewed adaptive password-hashing/account-lifecycle implementation.
findings.recommendation: Keep first-party identity mapping/JWKS and planned mature identity provider rather than merging this password system.

findings.title: Blender conversion generates Python source from raw path strings
findings.detail: fbx_to_glb_headless interpolates input/output paths directly into quoted Python source, then invokes Blender --python; special path characters could alter generated script. No exploit or converter execution performed.
findings.recommendation: Pass data through safe serialization/arguments in a reviewed isolated Blender worker, not raw source interpolation; use sandboxed file parsing.

findings.title: Incomplete/placeholder reference contracts cannot substantiate finished features
findings.detail: Base model contracts return fabricated output names/success-shaped dictionaries without making artifacts; actual concrete adapters override much of this. Missing 11 submodule source trees and weights block runtime. At least test_basic_endpoints imports nonexistent api.main.
findings.recommendation: Inventory adapters as meaningful research implementation, not validated product capability; never install base contracts as a working generator or declare tests passed without running an approved target.

findings.title: Redis result expiration targets a different key
findings.detail: complete_job hsets result into shared results_hash_key then expires results_hash_key:job_id, a different key. Static evidence indicates TTL may not apply as intended; no runtime Redis test executed.
findings.recommendation: Do not replace first-party durable store/worker with this reference queue. If adopted for private scheduling, design atomic claims, per-job retention and interruption behavior with meaningful tests.

findings.title: Top-level licenses do not clear bundled native dependencies/assets
findings.detail: diso embedded CC BY-NC4.0; Kaolin includes NVIDIA LICENSE.NSCL noncommercial terms in addition to Apache metadata. Three TripoSR transformer files preserve Apache-2.0 notices plus MIT modification notices. Supplied example bundle provides no license evidence.
findings.recommendation: Preserve every notice and RESEARCH_ONLY status; obtain review of source/weights/data/transitive/native chain before commercial integration.

secondary_findings: 3DAIGC config declares enabled text/image generation, painting, segmentation, auto rigging, learned retopology, UV unwrap and local text/image editing; these are inactive upstream-reference capabilities, not first-party product evidence.
Reference GPU adapter tests may execute real models; shared API tests use mocks, and some imports refer to missing api.main. Existence of tests is not a successful run.
11 declared upstream submodules and model weights are absent; Dockerfiles refer to additional absent native wheels. Reference snapshot is not self-contained.
Unsafe public defaults and mutable dependency/download operations require redesign/review before any deploy; no inference of maliciousness.
First-party qualification preparation should remain canonical for TripoSR; it intentionally removes stock hidden downloads/marching-cubes ambiguity and hardens checkpoint load.
Source licenses and old performance claims do not prove complete dependency/weight/data/commercial clearance or current measured performance.
Three TripoSR transformer files explicitly retain Apache-2.0 Hugging Face notices plus MIT modification notices; top-level MIT alone is an incomplete per-file license description.
Download helper verification labels refer to file size/count/presence rather than cryptographic integrity; do not reuse them as trusted artifact verification.

FastAPI application main entry point - Multi-Worker Configuration

This version is designed for multi-worker deployment with a separate scheduler service.

Architecture:
    - Multiple FastAPI workers handle HTTP requests
    - Jobs are submitted to Redis queue
    - Separate scheduler service (scheduler_service.py) processes jobs
    
Deployment:
    1. Start Redis: docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest
    2. Start scheduler: python scripts/scheduler_service.py
    3. Start API: uvicorn api.main_multiworker:app --workers 4

Key Differences from main.py:
    - No scheduler creation (connects to external scheduler via Redis)

files.module_doc:
IMPORTANT: FIFO Job Processing Implementation

This multiprocessing scheduler has been modified to implement strict FIFO (First-In-First-Out)
job processing with the following key behavioral changes:

1. **No Retry Mechanism for Resource Constraints**: When a job cannot be processed due to
   WORKERS_BUSY or NO_VRAM, it is immediately put back at the front of the queue instead
   of using a retry mechanism with exponential backoff delays.

2. **Strict FIFO Submission Order**: Jobs are submitted to workers in the exact order they 
   were enqueued. A job submitted later will NEVER be submitted before an earlier job 
   unless the earlier job is impossible to process.

3. **Job Failure Only for Impossible Cases**: Jobs are only failed if they are truly
   impossible to process:
   - No models available for the requested feature
   - VRAM requirement exceeds total available VRAM across all GPUs
   - Job has been waiting for more than 1 hour

4. **Resource-Based Requeuing**: When resources are unavailable, jobs are put back at
   the front of the queue and processing continues with a short delay to prevent
   busy waiting.

5. **Transient Error Handling**: Transient errors (network, timeout, etc.) cause jobs
   to be requeued rather than failed, maintaining the FIFO order.

6. **Concurrent Execution**: Jobs are submitted to workers in FIFO order, but multiple 
   jobs can execute concurrently on different workers. The scheduler continues dequeuing 
   and submitting jobs without waiting for previous jobs to complete, enabling true 
   parallelism across multiple GPU workers.

7. **Single Instance**: Uses singleton pattern to prevent multiple scheduler instances
   when deployed with uvicorn. For true multi-worker deployments, use external queue systems.

This ensures predictable, ordered job submission while maximizing GPU utilization through
concurrent job execution across multiple workers.

DEPLOYMENT NOTE:
- Use `uvicorn app:main --workers 1` for single-worker deployment with this scheduler
- For multi-worker deployments, consider Redis-based job queues or similar external systems

Standalone GPU Scheduler Service

This service runs the GPU scheduler and job processor independently from FastAPI.
This allows multiple FastAPI uvicorn workers to share the same scheduler.

Architecture:
    - FastAPI workers: Handle HTTP requests, submit jobs to Redis queue
    - Scheduler service (this file): Processes jobs from Redis queue using GPU workers

Deployment:
    1. Start Redis:
        docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest
    
    2. Start this scheduler service (single instance):
        python scripts/scheduler_service.py
    
    3. Start FastAPI with multiple workers:
        uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 7842 --workers 4

Usage:
    python scripts/scheduler_service.py [--redis-url REDIS_URL] [--log-level INFO]

Comprehensive Test Client for 3D Generative Models API

This script tests all available models and features using example assets from the assets directory.
It uploads files to the server, submits jobs, monitors their progress, downloads results, and saves them to organized directories.

Features tested:
- Text-to-textured-mesh (TRELLIS)
- Text-mesh-painting (TRELLIS)
- Image-to-textured-mesh (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D)
- Image-mesh-painting (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D)
- Image-to-raw-mesh (Hunyuan3D, PartPacker)
- Mesh segmentation (PartField)
- Auto-rigging (UniRig)

Execution Modes:
- Concurrent (default): Submit all jobs first, then monitor all jobs until completion
- Sequential: Submit and wait for each job one by one

Usage:
    # Concurrent mode (default)
    python tests/run_test_client.py --server-url http://localhost:7842

    # Sequential mode
    python tests/run_test_client.py --server-url http://localhost:7842 --sequential
